description: V3: locked geographic layout, independent procedural artwork, and data-driven gameplay content with stable IDs for quests, dialogue, NPCs, loot and encounters.
note: Compact hub, hotbar, faction agents, painted terrain blend, lore creature art

hub.name: Salvager’s Rest
hub.desc: A protected salvage quarter on the INNER Saltwatch Harbor waterfront. North is the secure city road; the southeastern controlled passage leads to Outer Quays.

quays.name: The Outer Quays
quays.desc: Ruined dock district east and seaward of Salvager’s Rest. Same coastal orientation: north is inland, south is the sea. West Passage reconnects to the Salvager’s Rest southeast gate.

nodes.text: You heading beyond the seawall? The storm left more wreckage than we can count.

choices.text: My equipment was lost. Can I borrow a basic kit?

nodes.text: An empty skiff came home without its crew. Find the mooring tag and come back with it.
Good. The West Passage is clear. Don’t count on the lower roads staying dry.
Low tide opens the lower quays. Rising water closes the cart track. Storm Gate stays reachable inland.
The harbor cannot replace what you lost. Take a worn arbalest and six bolts—but come back alive this time.
In this harbor we write the lost twice: once at home quay, once in the pilot ledger. The copies disagree.
Find the second ledger in the Customs Warehouse. I need the original, not another rumor.
Bring it back intact. Names matter here.
If these entries are true, someone altered the salvage records after the storm.
Then the unmarked cargo must be traced.
Dry rope costs less than a drowned salvager. What supplies do you need?
Rations, bandages, oil. Count your weight before leaving.
Don’t drag every crate home. Take the things that keep you alive.
Pressure seals are delicate. A dirty launcher is worse than no launcher.
That fitting came from an experimental batch. I’d test it before trusting it.
The sea strips heat faster than courage. Let me see your wounds.
Keep your bandages dry. Salt water is no friend to an open wound.
Past this gate is Saltwatch proper. Salvagers use the controlled passage to the southeast.
The city is not accessible in this prototype.
Wreckers say the Drowned King sank half the missing ships. Too convenient a story.
There are false sightings every storm season. Follow the paperwork, not the sea tales.
Start with the ruined Watch Store. Someone wanted the records gone.
The salt eats poorly spun rope. Keep your lines dry and double-knot them.
Check the tide markers before leaving the harbor. There is always an inland route home.
Old pressure seals need careful maintenance. I would rather fix a launcher than explain a failure.
Storms leave cargo everywhere. They also leave wreckers; mind who you trust.

quests.title: The Empty Skiff
quests.summary: A vessel returned without its crew. Recover its mooring tag and report to the dockmaster.

stages.description: Speak to Mara Fen at the Rest Docks
Recover the mooring tag near the Outer Quays boathouse
Return the tag to Mara Fen

quests.title: The Second Record
quests.summary: The official list of lost sailors contradicts its pilot copy.

stages.description: Retrieve the second ledger from the Customs Warehouse
Deliver the ledger to Edda Voss

quests.title: Cargo Without a Name
quests.summary: Follow a manifest for cargo that officially never existed.

stages.description: Collect the unmarked manifest at Customs

quests.title: Below the Waterline
quests.summary: Search tidal-cave debris for evidence of the missing salvage party.

stages.description: Investigate the Salt Widow cave marker
Recover evidence from the cavern cache
Extract and return to Mara Fen

quests.title: A False King’s Wake
quests.summary: Investigate misleading Drowned King reports around Saltwatch. The real catastrophe is not a routine local raid boss.

stages.description: Collect the false sighting report near the ruined Watch Store
Discuss the evidence with Talla Cor

factions.name: Saltwatch Harbor Compact
factions.description: Customs officials, reef pilots and harbor guards who protect the lawful port. Protect civilians and confront unauthorized wreckers.

factions.name: Licensed Salvagers
factions.description: Independent salvagers licensed to work the storm coast. Cooperate with Compact patrols but compete for salvage.

factions.name: Unlicensed Wreckers
factions.description: Unauthorized salvage bands willing to ambush crews and steal cargo. This is a working name for local hostile groups.

factions.name: Independent Harbor Crews
factions.description: Fisherfolk, repairers and independents who avoid violence unless threatened.
